'''Ruth King''' (née '''Langham'''<ref name=":1"/>) {{small|[[Fellowship of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]] [[Learned Society of Wales|FLSW]]}} is the current Thomas Bayes' Chair of Statistics in the School of Mathematics at the [[University of Edinburgh]], having held the position since 2015. Prior to this she held positions at the [[University of Cambridge]] and the [[University of St Andrews]].

Her main research interests are "Capture-recapture; [[Bayesian inference]]; hidden (semi-)[[Markov model]]s; [[State-space representation|state-space models]]; missing data; applications in [[ecology]] and [[epidemiology]]".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/school-of-mathematics/people/show?person=446|title=Ruth King {{!}} School of Mathematics|last=Building|first=Professor The University of Edinburgh The School of Mathematics Room: 4603 James Clerk Maxwell|last2=Buildings|first2=The King's|website=www.maths.ed.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-06-05|last3=Scotl|first3=Peter Guthrie Tait Road Edinburgh EH9 3FD}}</ref><blockquote>Her research focuses on the development of novel statistical techniques applied to a range of different application areas, particularly within ecology, epidemiology or medicine. This research is often interdisciplinary in nature, relying on strong collaborative links with other researchers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/ruth-king/|title=Professor Ruth King FLSW FRSE|date=2018-03-13|website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref></blockquote>She was recognised by the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] as one of Scotland's leading female scientists in their exhibition<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theedinburghreporter.co.uk/2019/04/leading-scottish-scientists-celebrated-with-major-rse-exhibition/|title=Leading Scottish Scientists Celebrated with Major RSE Exhibition|last=Preece|first=John|date=2019-04-16|website=The Edinburgh Reporter|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref> and elected as a Fellow in 2018. She was also elected a fellow of the [[Learned Society of Wales]] in 2017,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/fellow/ruth-king/|title=Ruth King|last=Wales|first=The Learned Society of|website=The Learned Society of Wales|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://imstat.org/2022/04/22/2022-ims-fellows-announced/|title=2022 IMS Fellows Announced|date=April 22, 2022|publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
She graduated with a BSc in Mathematics with Statistics in 1998,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~rking33/|title=Ruth King's Home Page|website=www.maths.ed.ac.uk|access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref> and completed a PhD in 2001,<ref name="Ruth King">{{Cite web|url=https://www.turing.ac.uk/people/researchers/ruth-king|title=Ruth King|website=The Alan Turing Institute|language=en|access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref> both from the [[University of Bristol]].<ref name=":0"/> In her final year of undergraduate she was awarded the 'Henry Ronald Hasse Prize'.<ref name=":1" /> Her PhD was supervised by [[Steve Brooks (statistician)|Steve Brooks]].<ref name="Ruth King"/>

Following her PhD she worked as a research associate at the University of Cambridge, from 2001 to 2003.<ref name=":0" />

From 2003 to 2005, she was an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|EPSRC]] post-doctoral fellow.<ref name=":0" />

From 2003 to 2010, she was a lecturer in Statistics at the University of St Andrews, then a reader in Statistics from 2010 to 2015.<ref name=":0" />

Currently, she is the Thomas Bayes' Chair of Statistics at the University of Edinburgh, a post she has held since 2015.<ref name=":0" />

She has spoken at numerous Conferences, in a number of countries, throughout her career.<ref name=":0" />

In 2019, she co-organised the [[International Centre for Mathematical Sciences|ICMS]] workshop on "Addressing Statistical Challenges of Modern Technological Advances" as well as the "Global Expert Working Group on Multiple Systems Estimation of Modern Slavery" in Edinburgh.<ref name=":0" />

She has 69 publications on "Google Scholar" since 2001, with a total of 1370 citations since 2014 (as of June 2019), and 2213 citations overall.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?hl=en&user=ESLfcHEAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate|title=Ruth King - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.co.uk|access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref>

Since 2017 she has been part of the team delivering the University of Edinburgh's  'Unlocking the World of Data' course on [[edX]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statistics: Unlocking the World of Data |url=https://www.edx.org/learn/data-analysis/the-university-of-edinburgh-statistics-unlocking-the-world-of-data |access-date=2023-09-13 |website=edX |language=en}}</ref>
